findings.title: Test reader thread is not joined before assertion
findings.body: The new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` starts a background reader thread with `new Thread(...).start()` but never joins it. After the main thread deletes all groups it sets `deletedAll.set(true)`, but the reader may still be inside a `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...)` call when the assertion runs. Any exception raised by that in-flight call (or by a subsequent loop iteration before the thread observes `deletedAll`) will be appended to `caughtExceptions` AFTER `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` has already executed, so the test will silently pass even when the bug it is meant to catch is still present. The reader thread should be stored in a local, joined (with a timeout) before the assertion, and `deletedAll` should not be set until after the reader is observed to have exited the read loop.

findings.title: Same NPE pattern remains on getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The PR only adds a null guard to `getSubGroupsCount()`, but the three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads immediately below (lines 256, 262, 268 in the head file) still use the exact pattern that was reported as NPE: `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)`. When the underlying delegate group has been deleted concurrently, `modelSupplier.get()` returns null and these methods will dereference null just like the original `getSubGroupsCount()` did. If the regression test is meant to prove the NPE is gone, it should cover these methods too, or the fix should be applied to all four methods (e.g. extracting the cached-load into a helper that returns null safely).

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount silently returns null instead of invalidating cache
findings.body: Before the change, `getSubGroupsCount()` would NPE on a missing underlying group. After the change it returns `null` without invalidating the cached entry, without going through `getDelegateForUpdate()`, and without calling `registerGroupInvalidation`. The other 'updated' paths in this class (`getDelegateForUpdate`, `isUpdated`) consistently treat 'group missing in DB' as `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")`, so this method now diverges from the rest of the contract: callers (e.g. `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`, which calls `representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())`) silently receive a `null` Long that may surface as a `null` field in the serialized representation. Either the cache should be invalidated and an empty/0 count returned, or an `IllegalStateException` should be raised like the sibling methods do.

findings.title: Regression test does not exercise the fixed code path
findings.body: The test only calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`, which lists top-level groups. The fix targets `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()`, which is reached through subgroup-count population (`GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`, only invoked when `subGroupsCount=true` is passed down). The listing call used here may not traverse the subgroup-count code path, so even if the fix were reverted the test could still pass by exercising only the un-fixed `getSubGroupsStream` paths. The test should either pass `false` for brief representation and use a parent group with subgroups, or directly invoke the admin endpoint that returns `subGroupCount` (e.g. fetching a single group with `?subGroupsCount=true`) to actually exercise the patched line.

findings.title: Reader thread is a non-daemon Thread without a name
findings.body: The reader thread is created with `new Thread(() -> {...})` and is not marked as a daemon. If the test fails or the thread is not joined (see previous finding), it can outlive the test method and keep issuing admin REST calls against the server after the test reports its result, polluting subsequent tests' state. The thread should be created as a daemon thread (or joined) and given a descriptive name so failures show up in stack traces.
